drhp.business: Hathway provides fixed line services through ISP and CATV to homes across pan-India, and is one of the leading fixed line internet service providers in the country, offering high-speed connectivity along with OTT offerings. It was the first Indian MSO to launch GPON FTTH and has 6.3 million home passes, a 1.02 million broadband subscriber base and approximately 91,000 kilometres of fibre optic cable. Its wholly owned subsidiary Hathway Digital Limited is one of India's largest Multi System Operators, running 2 main head-end facilities with 4 re-transmission centres over approximately 41,000 …

risks.note: The wireline broadband base declined to 1.02 million subscribers as on March 31, 2026 from 1.06 million a year earlier, so growth depends on ARPU and customer-quality improvement rather than volume.

Hathway Digital serviced approximately 4.63 million viewers as on March 31, 2026 'including through fellow subsidiaries and joint ventures', so a material part of the cable footprint sits outside the directly held entity; a restructuring exercise to simplify the group structure was undertaken during the year.
risks.risk: Cable television reach depends on fellow subsidiaries and joint ventures

risks.note: FY26 was an unusually challenging year on the external front with heightened trade uncertainty and penal tariffs; FY27 is expected to be a year of adjustment and the external environment remains uncertain, shaping the overall outlook.
risks.risk: Persistent uncertainty in the external / global environment

risks.note: The medium-term global outlook is described as dim with downside risks dominating; a protraction of trade conflicts would weigh on investment and further weaken global growth.
risks.risk: Downside-dominated global growth and protracted trade conflicts

risks.note: If the AI boom fails to deliver the anticipated productivity gains, it could trigger a correction in overly optimistic asset valuations with potential for broader financial contagion.

The 2026 US-Iran conflict and the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, affecting roughly 20% of global oil and LNG supplies, are driving surging energy and fertilizer costs, raising stagflation risk and cutting 2026 global growth forecasts, with India among the economies heavily dependent on Middle Eastern supply.
risks.risk: Energy security shock and stagflation risk

risks.note: Slower growth in key trading partners, tariff-induced disruptions to trade and volatility in capital flows could intermittently weigh on exports and investor sentiment, though these are characterised as manageable external uncertainties rather than immediate macroeconomic stress.
risks.risk: Trade and capital-flow volatility transmitting to India

risks.note: Inflation has moderated to historically low levels but some firming is expected going forward, and the forthcoming rebasing of the CPI series will have implications for inflation assessment, warranting careful interpretation of price dynamics.
